concerns.text: Circular label construction: FR-001 generates synthetic labels by rules keyed to motifs ('ester → hydrolysis, aromatic → photolysis'). The GNN is then trained to predict those labels from the same motifs, so SC-001's macro-F1 ≥ 0.70 on synthetic labels and SC-005's finding that IG highlights ester bonds for hydrolysis are true BY CONSTRUCTION, not empirical findings. The 'literature-based motif validation' fallback in SC-005 validates the labeling rule against itself.

SC-005 requires IG to identify ester linkages as top features for ≥90% of hydrolysis cases. When labels are synthetic (ester→hydrolysis), this cannot fail — the model only needs to learn the injected rule. The 'null distribution of shuffled motifs' with a two-tailed t-test does not break this circularity; the null comparison is against the same rule-generated data.

FR-010's external validation set of ≥30 'experimentally verified' records is the only non-circular evidence, but no source for such records is named, and the spec's own literature-gap analysis states no public dataset linking SMILES + conditions + observed pathways exists. If the external set cannot be assembled, SC-001's ≥0.70 on it is unachievable; the spec needs a named, verifiable source or a fallback that halts claims of empirical structure-mechanism findings.

Constitution VI mandates χ² validation at α=0.05; FR-006 replaces this with a permutation test, allowing χ² 'only for categorical count tables.' The permutation test is statistically preferable, but the spec silently deviates from a NON-NEGOTIABLE-adjacent constitutional principle without noting or justifying the amendment — this should be reconciled explicitly.

A two-tailed t-test against a permutation/shuffled-motif null distribution is the wrong estimator: permutation nulls yield an empirical p-value directly (as FR-006 correctly specifies for US-3). Applying a t-test to attribution scores across non-independent per-atom scores within the same molecule violates independence assumptions. Use the empirical permutation p-value consistently.
